summary.text: A 55-year-old woman with no significant past medical history was admitted with rapidly declining renal function after a normal serum creatinine at a check-up one month earlier. She had cough, vomiting, fatigue, oliguria, foamy urine and a 5 kg weight loss. Admission tests showed hemoglobin 79 g/L, serum creatinine 1106 μmol/L, albumin 35 g/L, hs-CRP 84.45 mg/L, 2+ proteinuria and 3+ hematuria; chest CT showed nodules, cavities and exudative lesions.

ANCA testing showed strong positive anti-PR3 and weak positive anti-PM-Scl antibodies, and serum immunofixation found an IgGλ monoclonal immunoglobulin. Renal biopsy findings were consistent with pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis, with weak kappa and lambda immunofluorescence staining. Bone marrow showed about 2% plasma cells, and flow cytometry about 0.12% monoclonal plasma cells. Immuno-electron microscopy showed no definitive light chain deposition, MGRS was ruled out, and PICGN with MGUS was diagnosed.

She received hemodialysis, intravenous methylprednisolone sodium succinate pulse therapy stepping down to 40 mg/day, and monthly cyclophosphamide 600 mg, then oral prednisone acetate 50 mg/day with tapering at discharge. Table 2 tabulated serial laboratory values on Days 1, 15 and 30, including hemoglobin of 79, 75 and 105 g/L.

During 3 months of follow-up serum creatinine stabilized at about 450 μmol/L, the patient reported anti-PR3 antibody turning negative, and free light chains declined. The monoclonal immunoglobulin became undetectable after treatment. Because the renal impairment was irreversible, she remained dependent on maintenance hemodialysis.

caption_evidence.quote:
Fig. 2.
Special staining for renal biopsy. HE staining: six glomeruli were observed, with no evidence of global or segmental glomerulosclerosis; PAS staining: focal tubular atrophy, interstitial edema, and scattered inflammatory cell infiltration were noted. Fibrosis was not prominent, and the arterial walls showed no significant thickening. There was no evidence of fibrinoid necrosis in the small arteries; PASM staining: granular degeneration of tubular epithelial cells was observed, along with red blood cell casts and occasional protein casts. Some tubules exhibited luminal dilation, epithelial cell detachment, loss of brush borders, and the formation of denuded basement membranes; Masson staining: six cellular-fibrous crescents were identified within the glomeruli, accompanied by fragmentation and collapse of capillary loops. Segmental fibrinoid necrosis was observed in one glomerular capillary loop.

caption_evidence.quote:
Fig. 3.
Immune electron microscopy of kidney. Glomeruli: glomeruli exhibit crescent formation. Focal vacuolar degeneration of capillary endothelial cells is evident. Occasional lumina contain aggregated erythrocytes. Significant endothelial cell hyperplasia is not observed, and capillary loops are patent; basement membrane: segmental thickening is present, with thickness ranging from approximately 250–550 nm; visceral epithelial cells: podocytes appear swollen with vacuolar degeneration. Extensive foot process effacement is observed. Scant subepithelial electron-dense deposits are occasionally noted; mesangial area: mesangial hypercellularity and matrix expansion are present. No electron-dense deposits are detected in the mesangium; tubulointerstitium: tubular epithelial cells show vacuolar degeneration. Occasional tubular epithelial cells are denuded. Mild increases in cytoplasmic lysosomes are observed in some tubular epithelial cells. Interstitial edema is accompanied by mild inflammatory cell infiltration; interstitial vessels: occasional capillary lumina contain aggregated erythrocytes.

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the four JPEG figures were inspected in the separate visual submission.
Table 2 cells shown as a dash are missing cells; no result is stated, so no observation was created for them. The footnote defines PLT but Table 2 has no PLT row.
Table 1 and Table 2 give no sample times beyond the Table 2 Day 1/15/30 column headings; Table 2 Day 1 is not equated with the admission text time point.

Fig. 4 prints SCr labels at D1 (1100) and D30 (281); 1100 is treated as a rounded label of 1106 (text and Table 2 Day 1 agree) and 281 versus the Table 2 Day 30 cell 283 as a source conflict (Day 30 cell review_only). Fig. 4 pixel labels, curves, day positions and symptom bars are kept in the visual submission, not as facts.

The Discussion says extensive fibrinoid necrosis while the Fig. 2 caption says segmental fibrinoid necrosis in one glomerular capillary loop; presence is recorded once as included and the two extent descriptions as review_only source_conflict facts.
Fig. 1 caption uses the undefined abbreviation LHCDD; not expanded.
The anti-PR3 antibody follow-up change was reported by the patient during a telephone follow-up; no assay value or date is given.
